title: An hour-long edit opens in a few seconds, not two minutes of a frozen app
goal: Opening the 20 minute reference edit freezes the app for about 14 seconds and the 60 minute one for over two minutes before anything can be clicked. A long project should open as quickly as a short one feels, with the window usable within a couple of seconds.
notes: Reproduced 2026-11-12 with the reference edit (task a-long-reference-edit-opens-in-the-probe-in-one). Command: Scripts/playtest.sh <copy of Scripts/playtest/reference-edit-opens-walk.json with setup referenceEdit 20 or 60 and expectTimeline lengthMS to match> --no-build. Output, the walk's log: 20 min (177 clips, 125 cuts): 'wait 2.0s, never went quiet ... mainBusy 18286.5ms over 883 passes, longest 13841.7ms from 48ms in'. 60 min (524 clips, 377 cuts): setup's open took ~140 s ('written in 145s', the write itself is under a second), then 'wait 2.0s ... mainBusy 181522.3ms over 3223 passes, longest 134942.9ms from 144ms in', walk ran out of time after 180s. 6 min (55 clips): longest pass on open 2.9 s. Likely suspects to confirm with a profile, not assume: the core's track layout is recomputed per call (trackLayout(), editPoints(onTrack:), editPointCut) and many callers ask per clip or per cut, so work grows with the square of the clip count. In the builder at 60 minutes, landing one clip with PhotonzDocument.land cost ~40 ms and setting one transition with setTransition(at: .edit) ~100 ms, so ReferenceEdit.Builder bypasses them; the timeline's views likely do the same per-clip asking.
acceptance: Opening the 60 minute reference edit (Scripts/perf/reference-edit.sh 60, or a walk with setup referenceEdit 60) leaves no main thread pass longer than 250 ms, and the window answers a click within 2 seconds of appearing.
The 20 and 6 minute edits open with no main thread pass longer than 100 ms.
Before and after numbers in the audit, measured on the reference edit.
